articles.title: Karnataka Defeat Railways by Three Runs to Win Maiden Women's T20 Trophy Title
articles.summary: Karnataka won their first-ever Women's T20 Trophy title after defeating defending champions Railways by three runs at the Narendra Modi Stadium B ground in Ahmedabad.
articles.content: Karnataka has pulled off a stunning upset to claim their maiden Women's T20 Trophy title, defeating defending champions Railways by three runs in a last-ball thriller at the Narendra Modi Stadium B ground in Ahmedabad. The Karnataka team made a brisk start with the bat, reaching 54/2 at the end of the powerplay, thanks in part to an impressive opening partnership between Shubha and Niki Prasad. The two batsmen put on 43 crucial runs for the second wicket, laying the foundation for their team's total. Shubha led from the front with a composed innings that proved decisive in taking Karnataka to 149/8. Her 39-ball 48 was a standout performance, one that showed her ability to adapt and thrive under pressure. The rest of the Karnataka batsmen also chipped in with valuable contributions. Railways' bowlers fought hard to keep their team in contention, with Poonam Yadav and Sneh Rana keeping things tight in the latter stages. Despite a strong effort from their top-order batsmen, Railways ultimately fell short, losing by three runs on the last ball of the match. Karnataka's bowling unit started strongly as Monica Patil conceded just six runs in her first two overs. She also managed to dismiss the aggressive Sneh Rana after being hit for two successive boundaries earlier on. This breakthrough was a crucial moment in the match, and it seemed to give Karnataka an upper hand. Back-to-back wickets in the eighth and ninth overs further restricted Railways' scoring rate, leaving them at 61/3 by the halfway stage of the match. The momentum had shifted firmly in Karnataka's favour, and they sensed an opportunity to push for a win. BG Tejashwini's dismissal of Minnu Mani in the 16th over added more pressure on Railways. The turning point came when BG Tejashwini returned in the 18th over and picked up two crucial wickets. She first accounted for Kaushalya Choudhary, followed by Arushi Goel, which swung the match decisively in Karnataka's favour. With a strong finish in sight, Shubha turned to Rajeshwari Gayakwad to defend 18 runs in the final over. Rajeshwari Gayakwad held her nerve and delivered under pressure, securing a memorable victory for Karnataka. The team erupted into celebrations as they tasted their maiden Women's T20 Trophy title. In an emotional interview with TOI, Shubha expressed her gratitude to the entire support staff, particularly head coach SN Ameet, who she credited with the team's success. The Karnataka team's maiden Women's T20 Trophy win has marked the beginning of a promising era for women's cricket in the state. Shubha expressed her gratitude to the entire support staff who contributed to their success. The KSCA Maharani Trophy T20 tournament played under lights at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium provided valuable exposure and helped the team cope with pressure, according to Shubha. She credited the competition for preparing them for the challenge they faced in the Women's T20 Trophy. KSCA president Venkatesh Prasad hailed the achievement as a phenomenal milestone for women's cricket in Karnataka, highlighting the importance of providing competitive platforms for female cricketers. The win demonstrates that with a good platform like the Maharani Trophy, results will eventually follow when players are given the opportunity to perform at their best. In recent times, some airlines have started rolling out new options and upgrades in economy, making flights more enjoyable without requiring a hefty price tag or points redemption. Airlines are revamping their in-flight entertainment offerings to provide passengers with seamless connectivity. The Wi-Fi experience on commercial flights is set to undergo a significant upgrade. Starlink, considered the fastest Wi-Fi in the sky today, is being installed or prepared for installation by several airlines. This cutting-edge technology will enable passengers to stay connected and entertained throughout their journey without interruptions. Ultrafast internet access is becoming increasingly available on flights. Sleeping comfortably while traveling coach has long been a challenge for many passengers. To address this issue, Emirates recently introduced its "U-Dream setup featuring adjustable side wings that support the neck during sleep. This innovative feature aims to reduce discomfort and promote restful slumber. Airlines are also experimenting with new ways to provide passengers with food and beverage options while in flight. Walk-up snack bars have begun appearing on some commercial planes, allowing passengers to stretch their legs and grab a bite to eat at 35,000 feet. United Airlines has opted to reserve the final row of its new Airbus A321XLR for a snack bar, providing passengers on long-haul flights in this single-aisle aircraft with an added convenience. Several major carriers have announced plans to introduce their own in-flight snack bars in the near future, indicating that this trend is likely to become more widespread in the coming months and years. JetBlue has been offering a pantry-style snack area on its longer-range planes for some time now, providing passengers with easy access to a variety of snacks and beverages during their flight. Some airlines are going even further by incorporating more comfortable seating options into their economy class cabins, such as United's upcoming Relax Row product, which features a couch-like setup designed specifically for families traveling together. Air New Zealand is set to introduce a new feature in its economy class cabins that could revolutionize long-haul travel: bunk beds. The innovative Skynest concept will provide passengers with two sets of stacked bunks, each three high, accessible via a ladder. This unique design allows for greater comfort and flexibility, particularly on ultra-long journeys where sleep is crucial. Passengers can book a four-hour nap in one of these cozy bunk beds for an additional fee of $495 - a small price to pay for a much-needed rest after hours of flying. The introduction of such amenities is part of a broader trend among airlines to upgrade their economy class offerings. Whether it's through more comfortable seating options or innovative features like bunk beds, passengers are being treated to a more luxurious experience without having to break the bank. articles.title: Windows Has Two GPUs: How to Identify Them
articles.summary: The Task Manager is one of the quickest ways to find out which GPU your system uses for certain tasks, but Windows offers other built-in options as well.
articles.content: When upgrading or troubleshooting your Windows PC, knowing the type of graphics processing unit (GPU) installed is crucial for making informed decisions. Many users don't realize that their computer can have two GPUs: one integrated into the CPU and another dedicated GPU, often from NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel, which handles demanding tasks like gaming. The system's performance and capabilities may not be entirely clear just by looking at an Intel or AMD sticker on the device. To identify the GPU in your Windows PC, you don't need to open it up or install any external software. Instead, there are built-in tools that can provide this information quickly and easily. However, these tools may only reveal details if they're not hidden in fine print. The Task Manager is one of the quickest ways to find out which GPU your system uses for certain tasks. But besides this tool, Windows offers other built-in options as well, which are useful when you need more detailed information about your graphics hardware. The Performance section of Windows' Task Manager offers a clear view into your computer's graphics card, including details about its memory, driver, and current workload. Windows labels GPUs based on their hardware location, not their performance, which means the numbering doesn't necessarily reflect the more powerful or primary graphics card. Below the performance graphs in Task Manager, you'll find dedicated and shared GPU memory. Dedicated memory refers to the VRAM available on a dedicated GPU, while shared memory is system RAM borrowed by the GPU when needed. Some integrated GPUs reserve a portion of system RAM for graphics, which Windows reports as dedicated memory, but an integrated GPU relies heavily on system RAM rather than having its own dedicated memory. Task Manager also provides additional details about your GPU, including branding, driver information, DirectX version, and even temperature readings if the hardware supports it. To view your GPU's name without any graphs involved, head to Device Manager by right-clicking the Start button and selecting it from the list. To get more detailed information about your system's graphics card, you can open the DirectX Diagnostic Tool from the Run dialog box. Pressing Windows + R will bring up the Run dialog box, where you can type dxdiag and press Enter to launch the tool. This will give you access to a range of tabs that provide details about your system's hardware and software configuration. The Display tab within the DirectX Diagnostic Tool provides information on the graphics card installed in your system, as well as its drivers, while the System tab shows the version of DirectX installed on your system. articles.title: Bison Jump Site Discovered in Texas Panhandle
articles.summary: Archaeologists have uncovered a rare example of a "bison jump" site used by Indigenous people for 3,000 years in the southern Plains region.
articles.content: Archaeologists have made a groundbreaking discovery in the Texas Panhandle, uncovering a rare example of a "bison jump that was used by Indigenous people for 3,000 years. This prehistoric hunting technique involved driving bison herds into a stampede off a cliff, much like being pushed onto a precarious platform. The technique has been long associated with the northern Plains, but this new find suggests it was also practiced in the southern Plains. In fact, only one such site had previously been identified in the region. Researchers have published their findings online, highlighting the significance of bison jumping" as a uniquely North American hunting method that produced some of the most productive food-gathering events in human history. The technique allowed hunters to channel bison herds into a controlled environment where they could be easily hunted and processed for meat. The newly discovered site, Nighthawk, is located within Caprock Canyons State Park and has been found to have been used by Indigenous people for an astonishing 3,000 years. This prolonged use of the site suggests that hunters had a deep connection with this hunting facility. The Nighthawk bison jump site in Texas is a unique archaeological find that has been discovered beneath a 65-foot-tall cliff spur. Archaeologists investigating the area found chipped stone tools and arrowheads near the bones of hundreds of bison that had accumulated at the site. Cut marks on some of the bison bones indicate that they were butchered using stone tools, suggesting that this was a prehistoric hunting practice rather than simply a natural death zone. The presence of these tools and butchery marks adds weight to the theory that Nighthawk is indeed a bison jump site, where hunters would herd animals off the cliff for food. Excavations at Nighthawk, a bison jump site in Texas' Caprock Canyons State Park, have uncovered evidence that challenges long-held assumptions about when and how Indigenous people harvested bison for food. Recent research suggests that these events were not limited to the fall season as previously thought. Instead, they may have taken place throughout the year, with each event involving a substantial number of participants - estimates range from 300 to 400 individuals. The sheer scale of such an operation would have required meticulous planning and coordination among the hunters. This is evident in the presence of butchery marks on the bison remains, which indicate that the animals were processed at the site itself rather than elsewhere. The Texan bison herding site's unique geography would have made it impractical to store large quantities of pemmican, a high-calorie food made from animal fat, which was likely too warm for such stores to last more than a few weeks. Instead, the southern Plains bison hunts may have served as a means to showcase power and build alliances among Indigenous groups. The rarity of kill events at Nighthawk, with an average of 500 years passing between each bison jump, suggests that the practice was not a regular occurrence. The fact that this technique was passed down over long periods rather than repeatedly revived is evident in the researchers' observation that the simplest explanation for the long-lived bison jumps is the consistent transmission of knowledge and skills across generations. The research reveals that despite their diverse cultural backgrounds, these early settlers shared a common approach to weaning their babies. The study's analysis of chemical signatures in children's bones found that infants began consuming solid foods at just three months old but were not fully weaned until around three and a half years later. This significantly longer weaning period than previously thought challenges the long-held assumption about ancient childcare practices based on written accounts from the time. Mothers' responses to their infants' needs played a key role in this extended weaning process, according to Laurie Reitsema, lead author of the study and a biological anthropologist at the University of Georgia. As a mother herself, she found it "exciting to uncover evidence of these mothers' adaptability and nurturing behavior from 2,500 years ago. Himera's early history is well-documented by historians: founded by Dorian and Chalcidian colonists in ancient times, the city grew into a thriving multicultural metropolis with inhabitants from various cultural backgrounds. The researchers analyzed over 13,000 burials, a significant portion of which belonged to adults, revealing surprisingly low infant and child mortality rates in the ancient city. Children born into this diverse environment likely faced different cultural realities than their parents, setting the stage for future generations to bring about changes in culture. However, the specifics of these childhoods remain shrouded in mystery. To gain insight into how weaning practices unfolded in Himera, the team focused on carbon and nitrogen chemical signatures preserved within some inhabitants' bones. These isotopic markers provided valuable clues about the city's infants' dietary habits. The researchers found that nitrogen levels rose during nursing until a baby's signature resembled that of a carnivore. Carbon analysis revealed what plant-based solid foods babies consumed once they stopped relying solely on milk, highlighting distinct differences between breastfed and weaned infants. A total of 58 children's and 27 adult women's bones were examined by the team. Their findings showed that Himera's children began weaning around 3 months old, earlier than recommended by ancient physicians like Galen and Soranus, who advised around 2 to 3 months later. Breastfeeding continued for nearly four years in ancient Himera, a practice that was much longer than what was recommended by physicians of the time. The prolonged breastfeeding period may be linked to the low infant mortality rate in Himera, according to researchers who analyzed chemical signatures from human remains found at the archaeological site. This extended nursing period is contrary to what Galen and Soranus suggested, who advised weaning between 1.5 years and three years of age. It's well established that breastfeeding has a significant impact on infant survival," Reitsema pointed out, particularly in societies where access to clean drinking water was limited. The findings suggest that even distant Greek communities shared similar approaches to breastfeeding, which contrasts with other studies in Roman cities where weaning practices were more varied and diverse. Chemical signatures extracted from ancient infant remains at Himera have provided a unique insight into the lives of these individuals, allowing researchers to reconstruct their early diets. The study's authors suggest that this approach can help identify patterns in child care practices across different cultures and time periods. This information is crucial for understanding how people lived together and interacted with one another. The researchers are now planning to extend their investigation to the adults who lived at Himera, recognizing that these individuals would have had unique experiences shaped by their childhoods. By examining the chemical signatures of adult remains, the team hopes to gain a more comprehensive understanding of daily life in this ancient Greek colony. Further analysis of the data may also shed light on how different cultural traditions blended together or remained distinct within the community, offering valuable insights into the dynamics of everyday life at Himera. Further analysis of the data may provide a more detailed understanding of how infants in ancient Himera transitioned from breast milk to solid food. Chemical signatures found in tooth enamel samples suggest that babies in this Greek colony began consuming solid foods at around three months old. The extended nursing period, which lasted nearly four years, indicates that mothers in Himera prioritized breastfeeding as a primary source of nutrition for their children. This practice is consistent with the cultural values of ancient Greece, where breastfeeding was highly valued and considered essential for infant development. articles.summary: A recent sketch on Saturday Night Live has touched on pressing issues within the American caregiving system, including the burden and costs borne by caregivers.
articles.content: A recent sketch on Saturday Night Live has resonated with millions of viewers who see themselves in its portrayal of family caregiving. The parody ad for "Sister," a fictional live-in elder care provider that's both free and your sister, has become a viral sensation on social media. The humor may be biting, but it touches on pressing issues within the American caregiving system: who bears the burden, what are the costs to them, and how will these demands continue to rise? Statistics paint a concerning picture: according to research by AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving, nearly one in four adults in the US, roughly 63 million people, have provided ongoing care to an adult or child with a medical condition or disability within the past year. This is a significant increase of 45% from just a decade ago. The number of caregivers has surged, and so too have their responsibilities: over 40% now provide high-intensity care, often involving tasks like administering injections and managing catheters, while only one in five has received training to do so. Caregivers face significant financial burdens due to the scarcity and high cost of paid help. The median monthly cost of a home health aide is substantial, at around $6,688 per month, leading many families to struggle with the weight of caregiving expenses. A recent analysis by the AARP Public Policy Institute found that working caregivers born between 1981 and 1985 are likely to lose substantial amounts in earnings, workplace retirement income, and Social Security benefits over their lifetime. This loss can be significant, with a typical caregiver in this age group facing a potential lifetime income shortfall of approximately $120,500, including around $15,400 in retirement and Social Security income alone. The cumulative effect of these losses is substantial, with estimated total lifetime income losses for working caregivers in this birth cohort reaching nearly $2.3 trillion. As caregiving responsibilities continue to fall disproportionately on women, research from the University of Michigan reveals a concerning trend. The number of years U.S. women can expect to spend caring for older family members or friends has increased by one year since 2011, reaching seven years. This disparity is particularly evident in care for parents and grandparents, where men's time commitment remains steady at four years. In contrast, eldest daughters are often the ones quietly propping up family finances, as noted by Edward Jones managing partner Penny Pennington. The cumulative effect of these losses on working caregivers' lifetime income has been substantial, with estimated total losses reaching nearly $2.3 trillion. The issue is not just a personal concern but also a societal one, as Gross emphasizes in his statement. The U.S. Census Bureau projects that by 2029, Americans aged 65 and older will outnumber those under 18, further amplifying the demand for care. articles.title: Federal appeals court blocks Army plan to detonate lead azide at Iowa plant
articles.summary: A federal appeals court has temporarily blocked the U.S. Army's plan to detonate nearly five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa.
articles.content: A federal appeals court has temporarily blocked the U.S. Army's plan to detonate nearly five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. The emergency permit authorizing this action was put on hold by the court, but the Justice Department is now suggesting that the Army could proceed without it. Government lawyers have filed a notice opposing an environmental group's motion to keep the permit suspended. According to the notice, EPA regulations allow the Army to take waste treatment measures in emergency situations where there is an immediate threat to human health or the environment, even without a permit. This provision is meant to be used as a last resort. The U.S. Army has not confirmed whether it plans to go ahead with the detonation, scheduled for November 23rd. An inquiry from reporters about this possibility was met with silence by an Army spokesperson. The Iowa Capital Dispatch reported that no comment was forthcoming on Friday. Iowa's Governor Kim Reynolds took swift action in response to the situation, activating the State Emergency Operations Center to coordinate state and federal agencies ahead of the planned blast. This move aims to ensure a unified response to any potential consequences. Earthjustice, an environmental advocacy group representing the affected parties, has expressed strong concerns about the Army's potential reliance on emergency provisions to bypass the permit suspension. According to Thien Chau, a senior attorney at Earthjustice, this provision is "an extraordinary and extreme backstop" that should not be used lightly. The court's decision has left residents in southeastern Iowa and western Illinois on edge, unsure if they will be facing a hazardous situation come Monday. A pause was issued by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit late Thursday, putting on hold the permit the EPA granted to the Army on November 13. This permit allowed for the use of material that posed an "imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment," according to the court's findings. The pause will remain in effect until the court rules on the emergency motion filed by the groups, which seeks to keep the permit on hold while it decides the case. The government has said it will submit its full response by Sunday. Cody Smith, director of climate initiatives at the Iowa Environmental Council, emphasized that detonating without court approval would be unlawful. The Army's storage facility had been holding 68 drums of lead azide for over two decades in a mixture of ethanol and water. This explosive material has undergone significant degradation and recrystallization, making it highly susceptible to damage from friction or shock. According to the Army's own maps, the blast is expected to release a cloud of dust containing lead particles that could travel up to 25 miles north of the plant. The Army had projected that low levels of airborne lead would disperse even farther. In light of this, some residents of Middletown were advised to vacate their homes during the blast. The permit governing the detonation requires the Army to model the dust plume using conservative assumptions, ensuring that any potential impacts are not underestimated. Nevertheless, the permit itself acknowledges that the modeling may not accurately reflect actual conditions, with EPA and Army experts expressing reservations about its representativeness. In an effort to inform the public about the planned blast, the Army held a public open house in mid-October. Just five days before the scheduled detonation date, on November 15, the Army released the detonation date along with maps showing how the dust plume would disperse. This move seems to have caught state and local officials off guard, as they only learned of the plans through a call from the Iowa Environmental Council on Monday, November 16. The governor's office has confirmed that neither the governor nor any state agency was informed about the planned blast before the Army's public announcement. The Army's decision to proceed with a blast has been met with resistance from environmental groups and lawmakers. A letter sent by Jim Macy, head of the EPA's Region 7 office, reveals that the agency issued emergency permits for lead azide between April and September, notifying state and local officials each time. The same letter also acknowledges the agency's approval of the detonation on November 13. This move has raised questions about the Army's decision-making process. A bipartisan group of lawmakers from Illinois and Iowa had urged a delay in the detonation, citing concerns over safety risks. Their letter to Telle and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin requested that an opportunity be given to explore safer alternatives. The officials expressed their reservations about the controlled detonation method chosen by the Army. The environmental assessment conducted by the Army considered several options for disposing of lead azide, including chemical neutralization. However, this approach was rejected due to concerns over the risk of accidental detonation during handling. The assessment concluded that 7 to 22 days would be required to complete the process safely. According to Macy's letter, the Army also evaluated building a structure over the material or moving it to the plant's open detonation unit, but deemed these options too risky due to advanced crystallization. As a result, the only viable option was seen as a controlled detonation with extensive mitigation measures. The Army's plan to detonate a stockpile of toxic lead at an Iowa plant has raised concerns among environmental groups, who argue that less hazardous alternatives were not fully considered before opting for this drastic measure. According to Earthjustice, the decision was made without thorough examination of options that could prevent widespread dispersal and deposition of toxic lead. This approach is seen as inconsistent with standard protocols for handling hazardous materials. The Army's posting in September 2025 of a federal contracting notice outlining plans for "lead azide neutralization" at American Ordnance LLC's plant has added to the controversy. The notice did not provide details on the method, leaving many questions unanswered. The Army's environmental assessment revealed that degradation of the material was discovered as far back as March 2026, yet no clarification has been provided regarding the notice or the implications for public safety. Requests from concerned parties have gone unaddressed by the Army. Army spokesperson Justine Barati suggested that residents worried about lead dust on their property could simply hose it off, implying that the issue is relatively minor. However, experts argue that fine lead particles can persist in the environment and pose significant risks to human health. Iowa health officials concur with Earthjustice's assessment, stating that no safe level of lead exposure has been identified, making the Army's guidance on washing away lead dust "absurd" and potentially damaging. The EPA has been conducting on-the-ground testing in Middletown since November 16th to assess the water quality and surrounding watersheds. This testing is aimed at determining whether there are elevated lead levels that require immediate action. Homeowners reliant on public water systems will receive filters if the test results indicate a need for them, according to the EPA's contingency plan. With the court's decision looming, residents are seeking clarity on what steps they should take in case of a permit reinstatement. The outcome could be decided as early as Monday, with significant implications for the Army's project and local communities alike. articles.title: US White-Collar Employees Show Little Interest in Developing AI Skills
articles.summary: A recent survey by Seramount found that only 18% of Gen Z workers want to improve or develop their AI skills.
articles.content: A recent survey of US white-collar employees has revealed a surprising trend among Gen Z workers: despite being digital natives and using AI at nearly the same rate as older generations, they show little interest in developing their AI skills. The study, conducted by Seramount, found that only 18% of Gen Z employees want to improve or develop their AI skills. This is significantly lower than other age groups, with 36% of millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of baby boomers expressing a desire to enhance their AI abilities. According to Jessica Reif, an assistant professor at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School, younger workers may be hesitant to use AI due to concerns about losing control over their work. Using a technology that blurs one's own contribution to their work can feel especially risky for those with less experience in their field, she explained. The survey, which polled over 1,800 employees from companies with at least 500 workers, also found that 58% of Gen Z workers use AI in their current roles. This rate is comparable to that of baby boomers (60%), but significantly lower than the rates for millennials (63%) and Gen Xers (67%). The fact that Gen Z workers are using AI at a similar rate to older generations, yet show little interest in improving their skills, presents an interesting puzzle. As they move forward in their careers, it will be worth watching how this trend develops, or if it changes at all. As Gen Z workers navigate their careers, a significant number are concerned about the implications of using AI on their professional reputation. According to recent surveys by Seramount, nearly one-quarter of Gen Z employees worry that relying on AI could lead others to question their abilities, compared to around 10% of millennials and Gen Xers, and just 8% of baby boomers. This concern is reflected in the fact that only about a quarter of Gen Z workers feel comfortable acknowledging their use of AI for work tasks. The anxiety surrounding AI usage may be justified given some striking research findings. In studies involving over 4,400 participants, researchers discovered that employees who used AI were often perceived as less competent and diligent than those who received other forms of help or whose help was not specified. This negative perception can also impact hiring decisions, with managers favoring candidates who do not use AI, even if they themselves are frequent users. The research suggests that this bias holds regardless of the age of the employee being evaluated, but could have more significant consequences for those still establishing their professional credentials. The implications of this stigma on Gen Z workers are particularly noteworthy given their career stage and growth trajectory. A senior employee's reputation can be bolstered by their use of AI, providing a tangible record of results that can offset any doubts about their effort or ability. However, this advantage is not available to early-career employees who lack a comparable track record. The pressure to use AI at work has a flip side as well. According to a recent survey, nearly half of all professionals worry about being judged for not using enough AI on the job. This concern is even more pronounced among those who are less experienced, with 48% expressing anxiety about being seen as lacking in AI skills. Young workers face a particular challenge: they must demonstrate their ability to work effectively with AI while also showcasing their individual capabilities. This dual expectation can create a daunting situation for Gen Z employees who are just starting out in their careers. Interestingly, younger workers appear less convinced of the benefits of using AI at all. According to one survey, only 30% of Gen Z employees believe that AI helps them work more efficiently. In contrast, roughly half of older colleagues share this view. A significant proportion of young people also question whether the immediate benefits of AI use come at a cost to their long-term development. One survey found that 80% of Americans aged 14 to 29 believe using AI tools is likely to make learning more difficult in the future. The hesitancy among Gen Z workers to adopt AI technology may be rooted in concerns about being judged by their peers and supervisors. This perception of risk could be a major obstacle for employers seeking to integrate AI into their workplaces, as it affects not only individual employees but also the broader organization's productivity and competitiveness. Despite growing concerns about job displacement due to automation, a significant portion of Gen Z employees are hesitant to develop AI skills in their workplaces. In fact, 48% of employed Gen Z respondents believe that the risks associated with AI outweigh its benefits, while only 15% think the opposite. This skepticism is partly attributed to inadequate preparation by schools, employers, and government for an AI-driven economy. However, the environments where young employees work may also play a significant role in shaping their attitudes toward AI. The lack of support from organizations can be a major obstacle for Gen Z workers seeking to integrate AI into their jobs. Only 27% of respondents in Seramount's survey reported that their employer provides help with AI adoption, compared to 38% and 43% among millennials and Gen Xers respectively. Younger employees are also less likely to seek assistance from colleagues when it comes to using AI tools. While 34% of baby boomers felt comfortable asking for help, only 18% of Gen Z respondents shared this sentiment. This could indicate that junior employees have limited access to enterprise AI tools or may not require them in their current roles. Research suggests that training is crucial for successful AI adoption across different generations. A significant difference was observed between employees who had received AI training and those who hadn't, with 93% of the former using the technology at work compared to 50% of the latter. The consequences of not engaging Gen Z in AI adoption could be far-reaching for employers. A depleted talent pipeline is a very real possibility if young workers are left behind in this technological shift. According to Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount, providing clear guidelines and training opportunities can help mitigate these risks. "If Gen Z falls behind on AI," she warned, "employers risk weakening their future leadership pipeline." This is a stark reminder that investing in young employees' development is crucial for long-term success. The disruption caused by AI could, however, also create opportunities for young workers to gain an edge over more established professionals. As OpenAI CEO Sam Altman sees it, rapid technological change can level the playing field and give those with fresh ideas and new skills a competitive advantage. Altman's perspective is not without merit, as periods of great upheaval often bring about new business opportunities. "I think you want to start your career at a time of the greatest change," he said during an interview with Stanford's Graduate School of Business in October. This sentiment highlights the potential for young workers to thrive in a rapidly evolving landscape. Altman emphasized that individuals with high potential, drive, and innovative thinking tend to do well when faced with significant change. He believes that having new skills and a fresh perspective can be a major asset during times of technological disruption. Demonstrating value beyond AI capabilities is crucial for employees to avoid being judged for using technology. Employees who communicate effectively about how AI enables them to contribute more or in ways that wouldn't have been possible may be able to counteract some of these negative perceptions. They need to show that they are proactive and can use AI to enhance their work, not replace it. Fortune : https://fortune.com/2026/11/21/gen-z-workers-ai-skills-seramount-survey/

articles.title: Politics Likely to Dominate Thanksgiving Gatherings
articles.summary: The recent midterm elections in the US are expected to influence holiday discussions, making it challenging for some individuals to navigate contentious conversations with loved ones.
articles.content: Thanksgiving is fast approaching, and given the recent midterm elections in the US, it's likely that politics will play a significant role in many holiday gatherings. For those who are weary of heated debates and tense conversations, finding ways to sidestep the issue altogether may not be feasible without sacrificing some personal relationships. However, opting out entirely can also have its drawbacks, particularly for individuals who value maintaining open dialogue with loved ones despite their differing views. A possible approach is to identify common ground by focusing on smaller issues that are tangentially related to politics. For example, even those with vastly different opinions might be able to agree on the humor in a particular politician's actions, such as New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani being spotted shoveling snow last winter. As Thanksgiving approaches, many people are seeking advice on how to navigate these kinds of situations without putting their mental health at risk. To provide some expert guidance, we spoke with Dr. Audra Nuru, a professor of communication and family studies at the University of St. Thomas in Minnesota, about strategies for engaging loved ones with differing views while also maintaining healthy boundaries. Preparing for potentially contentious conversations at social gatherings requires some strategic thinking. A good rule of thumb is to mentally prepare for the unexpected by anticipating sensitive topics that may arise. This involves taking a step back to reflect on your own emotional triggers and areas where you may feel strongly opinionated. Think of it as checking the weather forecast before embarking on a trip, knowing what's likely to come up can help you pack accordingly. It's essential to remember that everyone brings their unique experiences and perspectives to the table, making each gathering a rich tapestry of diverse viewpoints. By embracing these differences with curiosity and kindness, you create a more inclusive environment where meaningful connections can be formed. When navigating potentially toxic conversations, it's crucial to set healthy boundaries, think of them as having a reliable map and guide to help you navigate unfamiliar territory. When engaging in potentially toxic conversations at Thanksgiving gatherings, it's essential to prioritize maintaining relationships over proving a point. This means recognizing that the person you're interacting with is more important than winning an argument. As one expert advises, acknowledge that you may have different perspectives, this simple act can help others feel heard and understood. Listening actively requires more than just paying attention to what's being said; it demands empathy and a genuine attempt to comprehend another's viewpoint. To truly listen, try to understand the experiences and emotions that have shaped their beliefs and values. What personal anecdotes or events might be driving their opinions? By doing so, you can begin to see things from their perspective. In the midst of heated discussions, it's easy to get caught up in trying to convince others of your point of view. However, taking a step back and acknowledging shared experiences or common ground can help shift the focus away from conflict and towards connection. This might involve finding areas where you have mutual interests or values, even if you disagree on specific issues. Sometimes, giving yourself (and others) space to recharge can help prevent feelings of overwhelm and frustration from escalating into all-out conflict. By acknowledging and expressing our own emotions, we can create a safe space for others to share their perspectives without feeling attacked or judged. This empathetic approach allows us to navigate difficult conversations with respect, even when opinions clash. Using "I" language is an effective way to convey this message, as it shifts the focus from blame to personal experience and feelings. By doing so, we open up opportunities for others to own their emotions and engage in a more constructive dialogue, ultimately fostering bridges of understanding that can help us connect even in disagreement. articles.title: Stewart Rhodes says allegiance to Donald Trump is over
articles.summary: The founder of the right-wing militia group Oath Keepers has criticized several of former President Donald Trump's decisions and actions, including his decision to pursue war with Iran and his handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case.
articles.content: The founder of the right-wing militia group Oath Keepers has made it clear that his allegiance to Donald Trump is over. Stewart Rhodes, a staunch supporter of the former president, now considers him one of the worst in the nation's history. While serving time for his role in the January 6 attack on the US Capitol, Rhodes got a tattoo of Trump's defiant face after surviving an assassination attempt in Pennsylvania. This gesture was seen as a testament to his unwavering devotion to Trump at the time. However, that's no longer the case. "I am absolutely done with Trump," Rhodes stated bluntly outside a gastropub in Irving, Texas, where he was sitting at a rickety yellow table. His words are all the more striking given his past actions and statements, particularly his conviction for seditious conspiracy after orchestrating an attempt to keep Trump in power six years ago. Rhodes initially claimed that Trump's loss in the 2020 presidential election was due to widespread election fraud. However, when asked this year about the reasons behind a notable shift in Republican fortunes in Texas, he offered a different explanation for the party's struggles. As Stewart Rhodes mingled with supporters at a Christian Warriors After-Party, his black cowboy hat cast a shadow over his face. An eye patch covered the socket left vacant by an old gun accident, but his piercing blue iris remained visible. People gathered around him, shaking hands and signing up for Oath Keepers training sessions or community defense programs. The three-day "Christ is King: America After Trump" conference had brought them together, and now they were celebrating into the evening. The turning point in Rhodes' relationship with Donald Trump came when the president issued pardons to hundreds of individuals involved in the January 6, 2021, events, but spared his own sentence. This selective clemency left a lasting impression on Rhodes. Rhodes also criticized Trump's decision to pursue war with Iran, which he saw as a betrayal of the president's promise to end foreign conflicts. Furthermore, Trump's dismissal of those urging him to release files related to the Jeffrey Epstein case was perceived as an affront by Rhodes. Trump's actions were seen as a departure from his campaign slogan "Drain the swamp, which had resonated with voters who elected him to root out corruption in Washington. According to Rhodes, however, Trump's administration has been one of the most corrupt in U.S. history, marked by pay-for-play pardons and transactions. The White House declined to comment on the matter, leaving many questions unanswered. Sam Jackson, an expert on anti-government extremism at the University at Albany, suggests that the Oath Keepers' shift in allegiance reflects a deeper understanding of the world as being driven by sinister forces. Rhodes' own background is telling - he graduated from Yale Law School and worked for former U.S. Rep. Ron Paul before founding the Oath Keepers in 2009 with a mission to resist what they saw as unconstitutional orders. Fueled by conspiracy theories about voter fraud, group members became increasingly radicalized, eventually aligning themselves with Trump's political movement and supporting his attempt to stay in office after losing the 2020 election. Stewart Rhodes' trial had been marked by allegations of his involvement in the January 6 insurrection. He claimed to be a political prisoner" facing "illegality behind bars, where he was serving an 18-year sentence. U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta wasn't convinced by Rhodes' claims, stating that he posed a significant threat due to his charisma and persuasive abilities. The judge warned that upon release, Rhodes would be ready to take up arms against the government. From prison, Rhodes watched as Trump began his political resurgence. He witnessed on television the aftermath of the assassination attempt in Butler, where Trump rallied supporters with cries of fight. Rhodes believed God's hand was guiding Trump at this moment. The Oath Keepers founder saw hundreds of people convicted for their roles in January 6 incidents receive pardons from Trump after his 2024 election win. Rhodes himself received a commutation, but it didn't erase his record entirely. Rhodes claimed he was grateful when Trump allowed him to be released from prison. However, he noted that while some former Oath Keepers were pardoned, others remained convicted, including those who had assaulted law enforcement officers. Oath Keepers founder Stewart Rhodes has made it clear that his relationship with former President Donald Trump is irreparably damaged. Rhodes feels betrayed by the Republican Party's treatment of him, believing they've taken him for granted and offered him a choice between a half a dose of poison or a full dose". articles.title: Mosquitoes bred to carry Wolbachia bacteria show significant reduction in dengue infections
articles.summary: A study in Brazil found a 69% decrease in dengue cases among children living in areas with Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes, even during a severe outbreak in 2024.
articles.content: New research offers a promising solution to combat dengue infections: breeding mosquitoes that cannot transmit the virus. A major study conducted in one of the world's most affected areas, Brazil, has provided strong evidence for this approach. The researchers tracked over 5,700 schoolchildren living in neighborhoods where Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes were present and found a significant reduction in dengue and chikungunya infections. The findings show that these special mosquitoes led to about a 69% decrease in the number of cases among the children compared to similar areas without them. This effect persisted even during Brazil's severe dengue outbreak in 2024, according to Dr. Sri Edupuganti from Emory University, who was part of the research team. The study's results were presented at a meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Experts are now considering how this new approach can be combined with existing methods to combat mosquito-borne diseases. Dr. David Hamer, a global health expert at Boston University, believes that using Wolbachia mosquitoes alongside other measures could significantly reduce dengue cases in many areas. Florida is currently battling a significant outbreak of dengue fever, which appears to be the largest in any US state since at least the 1940s. The majority of locally acquired cases have been reported in Hillsborough County, where Tampa is located. According to health officials, this county accounts for more than three-quarters of the over 650 locally acquired cases tallied as of Friday. Outside the US, a nonprofit organization has been at the forefront of developing an innovative approach to controlling dengue transmission. Scientists have discovered that by breeding mosquitoes to carry a specific bacteria called Wolbachia, they can significantly reduce the insects' ability to transmit certain viruses. This approach is based on the fact that Wolbachia is harmless to humans but naturally occurs in many other insects. Field trials and studies conducted in Indonesia and elsewhere have demonstrated the effectiveness of this strategy in lowering dengue diagnoses. Preliminary results from the four-year study indicate that neighborhoods where Wolbachia mosquitoes were released had significantly lower dengue diagnoses compared to areas without these specially bred insects. While it remains unclear whether the Wolbachia mosquitoes have an impact on Zika cases due to their rarity in the area, researchers are optimistic about the potential of this strategy to combat dengue fever. articles.content: The Democratic Party's incoming senators are facing a critical test of their campaign promises to bring change to Washington. As they prepare to take office, the new Democrats are being forced to decide who will lead their majority in the Senate, a decision that is already sparking tension and controversy within their ranks. The 13 new members are part of one of the largest incoming Senate classes in decades, with several winning seats in traditionally Republican strongholds by vowing to shake up the status quo. Meanwhile, some Democrats from traditionally Republican states are taking a more cautious approach to the leadership vote. Annie Andrews of South Carolina has said she is speaking with both Schumer and Van Hollen, while Scott Colom of Mississippi wants to get to know them better before making a decision. Kansas Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton has announced he won't be backing Chuck Schumer for leadership, although he hasn't endorsed an alternative candidate yet. Hamilton emphasized the need for a leader who can unify people in his state and beyond. In Kansas, there's widespread discontent with the current political climate, which he believes Schumer may not be able to address effectively. The upcoming secret ballot vote on December 1 will likely see Schumer's long-standing relationships and experience with Senate procedures give him an edge. However, many incoming senators are hesitant to commit their support, creating a unique situation where first-term lawmakers might play a crucial role in shaping the party's direction. Mazie Hirono from Hawaii has called for embracing the new talent that's entering Congress, ensuring these voices are heard and valued. She believes these newcomers have fresh perspectives to bring to the table and should be given opportunities to contribute to the party's growth and development. As some Democrats in the incoming Senate class weigh their options for leadership positions, they are also making it clear what they do not want: business as usual. Their opposition to traditional approaches has led some to question whether these newcomers can deliver on their promise of change. Andrews' reluctance to commit to a candidate is one example of this hesitation. On a recent press call, she stated that she had made "no decision on the majority leader's race. Some Democrats are advocating for fresh perspectives in leadership positions. Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico believes that new faces are essential to revitalize the party and break free from stagnant thinking. However, he has not ruled out working with established leaders like Schumer. Iowa Sen.-elect Josh Turek is also taking a cautious approach, preferring to wait for more information before making a decision on leadership support. He has already met with both Schumer and Van Hollen, but says that his choice will ultimately depend on who best aligns with the priorities he campaigned on. Mary Peltola's thoughts on leadership are still unclear as she settles into her new role in the Senate. The Alaska senator-elect has yet to consider who will lead their party, despite being one of the newcomers who helped Democrats secure a majority. Progressive voices within the party are divided over which candidate should take the reins. While El-Sayed and Flanagan have been strong supporters of Van Hollen's leadership style, another progressive voice, Troy Jackson from Maine, has expressed reservations about Schumer's suitability for the role. The Senate's internal dynamics can be complex, with competing interests often at play. This makes leadership elections a delicate balancing act, one that requires a deep understanding of the caucus and its various factions. The leader must navigate these intricacies while also meeting the demands of party activists. Schumer's allies point to his success in navigating these challenges during his tenure as Senate Democratic Party leader. His efforts helped secure victories for candidates like Brown, Peltola, and Roy Cooper, who all contributed to the party's majority. The Democratic Party's base is growing increasingly restless, demanding bolder action from their leaders as they prepare to take control of Congress. Progressive organizations like MoveOn and Indivisible are urging senators to reject Charles Schumer's bid for leadership, citing a desire for more aggressive policies. MoveOn's executive director Joel Payne has emphasized that his organization's members want a new kind of leadership that will deliver on ambitious promises without delay or compromise. Our members are tired of politicians content with incrementalism - they want bold, creative leadership," he said in a statement. This sentiment is reflected in the vocal protests against Schumer at a recent news conference. The Senate leadership vote is being closely watched as a test of whether Democrats can deliver on their promises to bring about change. The party's progressive wing is pushing for more confrontational policies, including Medicare for All and restrictions on military aid to Israel. Van Hollen has positioned himself as a champion of these causes, promising an ambitious economic agenda and changes to the party's primary process. His supporters see him as a breath of fresh air in a Senate leadership that has been criticized for being too cautious. As the party navigates its leadership dynamics, some senators are weighing their options for future roles. Slotkin's backing of Van Hollen is notable given that she has also been critical of his progressive policies. This highlights the party's internal divisions and the challenges its leaders face in uniting their ranks. The outcome of this leadership contest will have significant implications for the party's direction, particularly as it looks ahead to the 2028 elections and the potential candidacies of senators like Jon Ossoff. articles.title: Earthquake Strikes Southern Africa in Area Thought to Be Immune to Tectonic Activity
articles.summary: A new study has found a rift zone in eastern Botswana's Kalahari Craton, contradicting long-held assumptions about continental stability.
articles.content: A powerful earthquake struck southern Africa in April 2017, sending shockwaves from the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. This ancient landmass is comprised of blocks of crust estimated to be up to 3.7 billion years old, considered too rigid and thick to tear apart by geologists. However, a new study has revealed that the craton is indeed being pulled apart by a rift zone, contradicting long-held assumptions about continental stability. The research, led by scientists at the Botswana International University of Science and Technology and the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, challenges the notion that such regions are immune to tectonic activity. According to the study, published in the journal Tectonics, this rift zone has attempted to fracture the craton before. The findings indicate that even the oldest continental cores can be susceptible to geological reactivation and subsequent fracture. The earthquake that occurred in 2017 was a significant event, as it happened in an area where no one expected tectonic activity to occur. Folarin Kolawole, co-author of the study and structural geologist at Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, notes that this region is characterized by "an active fault slipping," which contradicts previous assumptions about continental stability. The research highlights the complex geological history of the Kalahari Craton, with implications for our understanding of continental evolution. The study's findings will be explored further in subsequent articles, shedding light on the intricate processes shaping the Earth's surface over millions of years. The East African Rift System is slowly stretching apart at its southern tip, where a new rift has been discovered. This rift is in an early stage of development and could potentially split a continent open if successful, creating a new ocean. For decades, scientists believed the southern end of this system was located in the Okavango Rift Zone of northern Botswana, identified by geologist Christopher Scholz and colleagues in the 1970s. However, studies of the 2017 earthquake revealed that it actually reaches much farther south, into the craton itself. The discovery is surprising because rifts usually form around mountain belts, which are weaker zones where ancient cratons once collided. Instead, this new rift has broken across a craton, challenging long-held assumptions in geoscience. "It's counterintuitive, says Kolawole, highlighting the unusual nature of this finding. It basically challenges age-old thinking on how rifts form and propagate through continents. The team focused its research on the Khurutshe Fault, which cuts a 50-mile-long scarp across the Kalahari landscape about 50 miles south of the 2017 earthquake. In some areas, the land on one side of the fault is as much as 400 feet higher than the other. Researchers in Botswana excavated trenches alongside a major highway to study an ancient fault line that appears to be reactivating. They also analyzed data from water pipeline excavations and groundwater boreholes drilled across the region. These multiple lines of evidence all pointed to a common conclusion. The team's findings suggest that when a fault slips, one side of the land drops, creating a low spot where sediment accumulates and forms a wedge-shaped deposit. This process occurs as the fault moves, with sediments piling up against it over time. The researchers discovered that this exact phenomenon has occurred twice in the same area: during the Jurassic period, about 180 million years ago, and again today. Excavations at the site revealed more details about the ancient fault's history. Beneath layers of windblown sand, the team encountered hard, compacted sandstone from the Jurassic period, riddled with white calcite deposits that resemble a spider web network. These calcite veins were likely formed by hot fluids rising through cracks in the rock, much like those found at Yellowstone's geothermal springs. The fault's past activity has left behind a distinctive signature on the surrounding rocks. Some of the surfaces have been smoothed and scored by the repeated slipping motion along the fault line. This evidence suggests that the ancient fault was not just a static feature of the landscape but an active process that shaped the region over millions of years. Further analysis of the rock formations has provided valuable insights into the geological history of the area. The team's findings have significant implications for our understanding of how faults behave and interact with their surroundings. The ancient Kalahari Craton is home to a newly reawakened fault system, one that has been dormant for millions of years. A team of researchers has found evidence that this rift first formed during the Jurassic period, when Africa's landmass was undergoing significant stretching. A key characteristic of the Khurutshe fault is its location within the craton itself. The Kalahari Craton is an ancient and stable part of the African continent, but even these old blocks have inherent weaknesses that can be exploited by tectonic forces. The fault has offset young sand deposits that were laid down relatively recently. The rift's history suggests that it was initially formed during a period of widespread stretching in Africa. However, it failed to develop further and remained dormant until the East African Rift System began pulling on it once more. Exactly when this reactivation occurred is not yet clear. The researchers believe that existing weaknesses within the craton played a crucial role in the rift's development. Volcanic activity did eventually reach the area during the Jurassic, but faulting had already begun to occur before magma weakened the crust sufficiently to initiate the rift. This finding suggests that the rift exploited pre-existing zones of weakness rather than being caused solely by volcanic activity. The Khurutshe fault is still in its early stages of development, and it's not a new feature on the African landscape. The researchers note that breaking through to a new plate boundary can be a persistent process, requiring multiple attempts before success is achieved. The discovery has significant implications for the way southern Africa's tectonic plates are mapped. Some scientists have suggested that the region south of the Okavango Rift forms a single stable microplate known as the San Plate. However, an active rift with large earthquakes and fresh fault lines is located squarely within this supposed stable plate. We cannot assume that the plate is coherent," Kolawole notes, indicating that the San Plate may not be as solid as previously thought. The researchers propose that the San Plate could be slowly breaking into two smaller plates, which they call the North San Plate and the South San Plate. The breakup of a tectonic plate is a gradual process that unfolds over millions of years, if it happens at all. According to GPS measurements, the rifts in southern Africa are opening far more slowly than those found in other parts of Africa, such as Malawi, Kenya, and Ethiopia. Slow-moving rifts can stall or fail altogether, but Kolawole points out that plate boundaries often start slow before accelerating later on in their life cycle. Studying this rift as it begins to form offers a rare glimpse into the process of new plate boundaries emerging, potentially leading to Africa's eventual split. The African continent is home to some of the oldest landmasses on Earth, and scientists have discovered a rare phenomenon within one of these ancient territories. An ancient failed rift that had previously gone dormant is now reawakening, offering researchers a unique opportunity to study the process of new plate boundaries emerging. This event has significant implications for Africa's geological future, potentially leading to its eventual split into separate landmasses. The rift's formation and growth will be closely monitored by scientists, who are eager to gain insights into the complex processes that shape our planet's surface. articles.title: Mario Sorrenti Exhibition in Paris Sheds Light on Photographer's Personal Diaries
articles.summary: A recent exhibition at LSD gallery during Paris Photo showcased Mario Sorrenti's personal diaries from the 1990s, offering a glimpse into his life and relationships.
articles.content: A recent exhibition in Paris has shed light on the personal diaries of renowned photographer Mario Sorrenti from the 1990s, offering a glimpse into his life, relationships, and experiences behind some of fashion photography's most iconic images. The show, held at LSD gallery during Paris Photo, is an intimate journey into the world of a photographer who has significantly impacted how we perceive beauty, desire, and sensuality in fashion. The small gallery space was packed with visitors, mostly young people who seemed captivated by Sorrenti's handmade books filled with photographs, Polaroids, and handwritten notes. These objects are a far cry from the digital images that dominate our lives today, and it is clear that their physicality and tactility have sparked a fascination among this generation. I couldn't help but wonder what drew these young people to these tangible artifacts of a bygone era. Was it nostalgia for a time they had never experienced? The answer may lie in the way we interact with images today, increasingly through screens, devoid of the physicality and authenticity that Sorrenti's diaries represent. As I delved deeper into the exhibition, I began to notice something more profound at play: a longing for real experiences, for a connection with images that feels lost in our digital age. Mario Sorrenti is one of the most influential photographers of his generation, whose work has had a lasting impact on fashion photography since the early 1990s. His contributions to Vogue Italia are particularly noteworthy, with an extensive body of editorials that have shaped not only the visual language of fashion but also how it communicates desire and emotion. Sorrenti's photographs have helped redefine the aesthetics of fashion and paved the way for a more nuanced exploration of intimacy and emotion in his work. As I continued to explore the exhibition, I couldn't help but feel that there was something more to Sorrenti's diaries than just their historical significance or aesthetic appeal, they offered a glimpse into a life lived authentically. The young people gathered around Sorrenti's diaries seemed entranced by the fragments of his life, the Polaroids and handwritten notes offering a tangible connection to the past. It was as if they were searching for something more profound in these objects: a sense of authenticity that is increasingly elusive in our digital lives. Mario Sorrenti's photographs are instantly recognizable, even without seeing his name attached to them. His unique style cannot be reduced to a single technique or aesthetic approach, but rather it's a culmination of various elements that come together in his work. Light is a crucial aspect of Mario's photography, and he handles it with extraordinary sensitivity. Whether it's soft and natural or carefully controlled, light plays a pivotal role in setting the tone for his images. His attention to detail extends beyond just lighting, as he also focuses on skin texture, physical presence, and the overall body language of his subjects. One of Mario's defining characteristics is his ability to seamlessly transition between spontaneous, informal shots and more formally constructed images. This range allows him to capture a wide array of moods and emotions, from intimate moments to more dramatic scenes. His photographs often have a sense of authenticity that feels genuine and unforced. Sensuality is a key element in Mario's work, but it never feels imposed on his subjects. Rather, it emerges organically from the relationship between him and the person in front of his camera. Even when an image is provocative or pushes boundaries, there's often a sense of tenderness and vulnerability that prevents it from becoming overly suggestive. In fashion photography, desire has always been a complex theme to tackle. Mario wasn't the first photographer to explore intimacy or eroticism, but he brought a unique perspective to the tradition. His subjects are not mere bodies to be admired; they retain their individuality and interiority within the carefully constructed world of fashion. Mario's photographs have an uncanny ability to make us feel that something genuine is happening within the image. This quality is perhaps best exemplified by his work with Kate Moss, who was both his girlfriend at the time and a muse for many of his most iconic images. Their collaboration led to the now-iconic Calvin Klein Obsession campaign in 1993. The true power behind those photographs lay not just in Mario's technical skill or Kate's beauty but in the genuine intimacy that had developed between them. These were not staged moments, but rather a natural extension of their existing emotional connection. The resulting images have become an integral part of our collective visual memory, and they continue to captivate audiences with their raw emotion and authenticity. The Paris exhibition takes a different approach to showcasing Mario's work, one that delves into the world from which his photographs emerged. Instead of displaying the iconic images that solidified his reputation, the show focuses on the everyday life and personal experiences that inspired them. This is where the five diaries come in, handwritten notes, drawings, contact sheets, and fragments of daily life spanning 1991 to 2000. Each diary page has been meticulously reproduced using color Xerox machines and reassembled by hand into unique volumes. These are not traditional photographic books or mere archival documents; rather, they occupy a fascinating space where memory, artistic experimentation, and the physical act of creation blend together. As we flip through these pages, we're met with an array of faces, bodies, and moments from everyday life, friends, lovers, and familiar figures from the fashion world, all intertwined with deeply personal reflections on those around him. The diaries are not showcases for finished masterpieces but rather invitations into the process of becoming a photographer. Fashion photography has evolved to become more than just a means to showcase products; it's now a platform for artists to explore their creativity freely. These photographs are not standalone images but are deeply intertwined with Mario Sorrenti's life experiences, the people he loved, and the environments that shaped him. The diaries reveal the development of a unique photographic style that is inextricably linked to his personal growth as an individual. Living in New York during those same years gave me a unique perspective on this era. I share Mario's generation, having grown up amidst the city's vibrant cultural landscape. New York City in the 1990s was a hub of creative exchange where various art forms, fashion, photography, music, and nightlife, converged to create something entirely new. The atmosphere that pervaded the city during those years was characterized by an infectious sense of freedom, experimentation, and possibility, but also a rawness and urgency. Photography was more than just a job for Mario's family, it was a way they connected with each other and the world around them. This shared passion is evident in Mario's work, which often feels deeply personal despite being created within the high-stakes fashion industry. Davide's presence in the diaries adds an extra layer of poignancy to the images. Knowing his story transforms these fragments of a shared youth into something more, a testament to a relationship, love, loss, and a world that once was but now exists only through the photographs left behind. Photography has a unique relationship with time; it captures a moment while simultaneously reminding us that it's gone. In Mario's diaries, this dynamic is amplified as photographs are intertwined with words, drawings, other photographs, and fragments of thought, revisited, rearranged, reproduced, and transformed in a way that blurs the line between memory and creativity. The use of Xerox machines to reproduce images adds another dimension to the artistic language, making reproduction an integral part of the creative process rather than just a means of copying an original. Mario Sorrenti's diaries reveal a life spent observing and recording the world around him, a process that involved not just looking but also selecting, arranging, touching, and remembering the fragments of existence. The physicality of this creative labor is evident in the pages of his diaries, where time is measured by hours spent searching for the perfect image or moment to capture. This dedication to detail is perhaps what resonated with young visitors to a recent Parisian gallery exhibition featuring his work. Their fascination was not driven solely by nostalgia for a lost era; many had never experienced the world depicted in Sorrenti's diaries, yet they were drawn to its authenticity and imperfections. The allure of these photographs lies in their ability to convey the beauty and complexity of human existence, unvarnished by the conventions of art or photography. The exhibition at LSD, curated by Aaron Stern, offers a glimpse into Sorrenti's unique visual language, one that is rooted in his personal experiences and perceptions of the world. articles.title: Tech Outages Surge Worldwide Amid AI-Driven Security Shift
articles.summary: A surge in tech outages worldwide is attributed to the increasing influence of artificial intelligence on digital defense and security.
articles.content: Reports are emerging of a surge in tech outages worldwide, sparking concerns about the resilience of modern digital infrastructure. Experts say these incidents have routine explanations, but they also point to a growing trend: AI is increasingly influencing the dynamics of digital defense and security. Researchers attribute this shift to the proliferation of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery, which has unleashed a flood of software bugs that attackers are then exploiting with AI tools at an unprecedented pace. As a result, organizations face intense pressure to rapidly patch their systems, leaving IT teams struggling to keep up with the sheer volume of updates. The rapid pace of technological advancements has created a perfect storm for network failures. Flawed updates in infrastructure can have far-reaching consequences, as seen in Microsoft's recent 365 outage. A combination of factors contributed to this issue, including other network failures that exacerbated the problem. The NSA has also been affected by a similar issue. Its internal communication system went offline due to botched patching following critical PHP updates in October. This highlights the strain on systems caused by the need for rapid updates and patches. The consequences can be severe, disrupting essential services. Internal updates are also causing problems for other major tech companies. Apple has reported snafus related to an internal update, further underscoring the challenges of keeping pace with technological advancements. These issues demonstrate that even well-resourced organizations can struggle with the demands of maintaining secure and up-to-date digital systems. The accumulation of "tech debt, a result of cutting corners on upgrades and maintenance, has become a significant concern for many organizations worldwide. This practice, though often tolerated in the past, now poses a greater risk due to increased external pressures and bugs in patches. The increasing reliance on artificial intelligence (AI) in IT administration has led to a growing trend of accelerated evaluation and preparation for updates, but experts warn that human analysis and planning are still essential components of the process. While AI tools can provide valuable support, they cannot replace the need for human understanding of what went wrong and whether the patch addresses the underlying issue. In fact, many IT administrators are now relying on AI to augment their work, rather than automate it entirely. The use of AI in cybersecurity is becoming more widespread, but its limitations should not be overlooked. As one expert notes, current AI tools are still unable to replicate human analysis and planning, highlighting the need for a combination of both human insight and technological support. Despite these challenges, there is growing optimism that AI acceleration will eventually help defenders get on top of common vulnerabilities and better secure software in general, leading to a decrease in background noise and new security threats. The sheer scale of vulnerabilities being uncovered has reached a staggering milestone this week, with over 100,000 identified in 2026 alone. In comparison, just four years ago in 2022, there were roughly 25,000 recorded vulnerabilities, highlighting the exponential growth in the number of potential security risks. This year's total is even more striking when considered alongside previous years: it has already surpassed the combined totals for both 2024 and 2025, with still over a month to go before the end of the year. The recent disclosures by researchers using AI have shed light on critical vulnerabilities in a range of software systems, including PHP, NGINX, and Java. The recent spate of outages across various industries has highlighted a disturbing trend: the increasing reliance on software systems that are inherently vulnerable to bugs and glitches. Researchers have been warning about these vulnerabilities for some time now, but it seems their warnings are finally being heeded. Meanwhile, in another development, JPMorgan Chase has confirmed that hackers have breached its security systems in a separate incident. The attackers gained access to certain marketing data held by third-party vendors, which may include sensitive customer information such as names and email addresses. While the bank downplayed the severity of the breach, it acknowledged that some company data was stolen. Visa and Mastercard have also been affected by similar attacks against their vendors. It's a worrying trend that highlights the need for better security measures across the financial industry. The fact that these incidents are not linked to the recent outages is cold comfort, as it suggests that there may be more vulnerabilities waiting to be exploited. Police in the Netherlands have recently foiled several attempts at violence directed towards customers of digital bank Revolut. While the motives behind these attacks are unclear, they follow a disturbing trend of physical assaults on wealthy cryptocurrency holders who are forced to hand over money while being held hostage. A court ruling has compelled the UK government to acknowledge that it instructed Apple to bypass its own encryption and access customer iCloud data. This admission follows a long-standing dispute over the extent of government powers in accessing sensitive information.
